subject: Cerulean: token runway & compute orchestration for Phase 1
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir@cerulean.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya@cerulean.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@cerulean.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: kickoff: Phase 1 throughput targets and SOC

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the intro call today. As promised, I attached the initial traffic profile and a short note on what Phase 1 looks like for us. High level:

- 500k active users (alpha), expected 2 requests/user/day
- Average prompt ~220 tokens, average generated ~180 tokens
- Burst windows during business hours (US-EAST) with 3x traffic spikes for 10–15 minutes

Our internal SLA ask for Phase 1 is 500ms p95 for single-turn completions and an escalation path if p99 > 1s. We are flexible on sustained tail but need predictable headroom for spikes.

Can Redwood share a mapping of token/sec to expected GPU SKUs for a 99% availability target and a canary plan to validate latency under burst?

Appreciate it — Samir

[Attachment: cerulean_traffic_profile_v1.csv]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir@cerulean.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: kickoff: Phase 1 throughput targets and SOC

Samir — thanks for the profile, this is helpful. Looping in Ben and Karthik from capacity/ops to propose a solid runway and an orchestration plan that meets the p95 goal.

Quick summary of what we need to validate on our side:
- Baseline tokens/sec for your median and 95th percentile request shapes
- Acceptable cost tradeoffs for reserved vs burst GPU time (you mentioned monthly budget guidance on the call)
- Any required data residency or private deployment constraints (for canary)

Next step: Ben/Karthik to share a draft tokens/sec -> GPU SKU mapping and a phased validation plan (canary on hosted + dedicated reserved capacity for steady-state).

Thanks,
Kimberly
Director, Enterprise Sales\Redwood Inference
[Attachment referenced: proposal_draft_v3.pdf]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Samir Rao <samir@cerulean.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Cerulean Phase 1 — initial compute/throughput model

Samir / team — I ran the numbers off the traffic CSV and a representative model: opt-7b-llama-v2-quant (our sim profile). Assumptions up front: avg inference tokens = 400 total (prompt + generation), median seq = 220/180; batching/caching turned on for identical prompts during spikes.

Key estimates:
- Steady-state average demand: ~185 tokens/sec total across peak minute -> ~1.2k TPS (tokens/sec) 
- 3x burst spikes -> ~3.6k TPS sustained for 10–15 minutes
- Our bench: a single A100-80GB equiv provides ~950–1,100 tokens/sec for the chosen model under continuous batching with 30ms kernel latency; p95 latency ~420–520ms depending on batch hit-ratio.

Sizing proposal (Phase 1):
1) Reserved slab (steady-state): 2 x A100-equivalent nodes (provides ~=2.0–2.2k TPS), covers base demand with ~10–20% headroom.
2) Burst capacity (on-demand pool + pre-warmed standing-by GPUs): additional 2 x A100-equivalent nodes that can be added within 90–120s; with pre-warmed routing we can reduce cold-start to ~30–45s. Combined pool -> ~4 x A100 equiv = ~3.8–4.4k TPS, covers 3x spikes with ~5–15% headroom depending on batch efficiency.

Risk & mitigations:
- Tail latency at p99 during spikes: recommend a fallback policy to a smaller model (opt-3b-quant) for non-critical requests and a short-circuit path for re-tries.
- KV cache warmup: pre-warm by replaying a small representative prompt set during canary to prime caches.

Deliverables: I will attach a tokens/sec workbook with per-minute profiles and cost delta for reserved vs burst.

Next action: Samir — could you confirm acceptable p99 thresholds and any non-negotiable request classes (e.g., billing lookups must always be full-fidelity)?

-Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: cerulean_token_model.xlsx (sheet: TPS_estimates)]

From: Samir Rao <samir@cerulean.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@cerulean.ai>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cerulean Phase 1 — initial compute/throughput model

Thanks Ben — this is the level of detail we needed. A few clarifications from our side:

- p95 500ms is a hard ask for all customer-facing completions. p99 we can accept up to 1.5s for non-critical flows; critical flows (auth, billing, compliance checks) must stay under p99 900ms.
- Budget: Phase 1 monthly cap is $45k for inference (hosted + any dedicated reserve amortized).
- Compliance: we need audit logs for all requests for Phase 1 retention = 30 days; SOC2 attestation is in flight but we need to ensure log export is available.

Can we get a revised slab plan that guarantees the critical-flow tail SLA by either reserving higher-priority capacity or isolating those requests on smaller, lower-latency instances? Also curious on how much headroom we get if we swap to an H100-optimized runtime (we have a slight bias to H100 if it reduces p99).

- Samir

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir@cerulean.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 16:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cerulean Phase 1 — initial compute/throughput model

Samir — quick follow-up with a concrete revision and validation plan.

Revised numeric proposal (based on strict p95/p99 asks + budget constraint):
- Dedicated reserved: 3 x A100-equivalent (steady-state), pinned to Cerulean tenant. This yields ~3.0–3.3k TPS reserved and gives us a separate reservation for critical flows (isolate via route tags). Cost delta: +~35% vs 2-node slab but keeps critical p99 within 900ms at expected batch hit-ratio.
- Burst pool: 1 x H100-equivalent pre-warmed node + autoscale from hosted to add up to 2 more H100 equiv if spikes exceed 3.3k TPS. H100 path reduces kernel latency; expected p95 improves by ~15–20% in our runtime.
- Fallback policy: critical flows always route to reserved slab; non-critical can be rerouted to opt-3b fallback if p99 threatens 1.5s.

Validation / timeline:
1) Week 0 (canary): run 15-min synthetic spike replay against hosted + one reserved node to validate cache warmups and routing; measure p95/p99 and batch hit-rate.
2) Week 1: provision 3 reserved nodes and pre-warm with production-like prompt set (we will coordinate CSV replay).
3) Week 2: run a 1-hour soak with 3x spikes, capture audit logs and tail latency.

Deliverable: I attached a small comparison table in the workbook showing expected latency headroom vs cost for the 2 vs 3 reserved scenarios and an H100 uplift column.

Action items:
- Kimberly: confirm Cerulean’s preference on 3-node reserved vs 2-node + more aggressive H100 bursting (both meet different cost profiles).
- Samir: please confirm critical flow list and ensure we have the production prompt sample for warmup.
- Procurement: once plan chosen, we’ll send an amendment with slab sizing and reserved pricing.

Thanks — Karthik
VP, Capacity Planning & Runtime Optimization\Redwood Inference
